TEAM_DATA.name: Venom — Poison + Airborne
TEAM_DATA.note: Charlotte is the main damage dealer, Johnny adds Poison and Airborne as sub-DPS, and Reina is the Airborne enabler. Poison unlocks Illusion Kick and Poison Grab, and Airborne unlocks Venom Cutter, Shadow Grab, Tempest and Wind Grab, so every conditional skill stays live. This is the game's own recommendation for Charlotte. Alt: Eileen can take Reina's slot as the Airborne starter, adding +15% team Attack (Brave One) and +20% team Crit Rate (Vanguard Banner).

TEAM_DATA.name: Gale — Airborne + Burn
tags: Main DPS + Sub-DPS / buffer + Airborne enabler
TEAM_DATA.note: Kalsion is the main damage dealer, Eileen adds Airborne damage plus team Attack and Crit Rate buffs, and Reina starts Airborne. Three Airborne sources keep Explosion (2173%), Tempest, Wind Grab and Rolling Upper available. Matches the game's recommendations for Reina and Eileen. Alts: Charlotte as the damage dealer instead of Kalsion; Johnny (the game recommends him with Eileen; Poison and more Airborne) or Castella (Break starter) for Reina.

TEAM_DATA.name: Blazeflame — Burn + Airborne
tags: Main DPS + Burn / Airborne sub-DPS + Burn / Stun enabler
TEAM_DATA.note: Kalsion is the main damage dealer. Aria applies Burn and Airborne with almost every attack, keeping both of his conditions live (Burn for Burst Grab, Airborne for Explosion), and Kalien stacks Burn and adds Stun with Finale. This is the game's recommendation for Aria, Kalien and Kalsion. Not S because Aria and Kalien are B-tier damage. Alts: Cerese (the game recommends her with Kalsion; Frost and Airborne) for Aria; Reina as Airborne setup instead of Kalien.

TEAM_DATA.name: Bloodburst — Bleed + Stun
tags: Main DPS + Stun / Bleed sub-DPS + Stun enabler
TEAM_DATA.note: Roxy is the main damage dealer, Theresia applies Stun and Bleed and hits hard on Stunned foes, and Astria adds a third Stun source with Precision Shot. Three Stun sources (Celestial Verdict, Crimson Spiral, Precision Shot) keep Kick Storm (1786%), Divine Arc and Bolt Bombard live. This is exactly the game's recommendation for Roxy and Theresia, and it is close to S with Merciful Death Sentence. Alt: Lute (healer, Stun from Stun Slash) for Astria.

TEAM_DATA.name: Thunderbolt — Shock
tags: Main DPS / healer + Shock sub-DPS + buffer
TEAM_DATA.note: Tarte is the damage slot (Shock, Stun and a conditional heal from Cure), Ornette adds Shock control, Knockdown and +30% Crit Damage for herself, and Sion buffs the team with +15% Attack or Defense (Bless). All three apply Shock and turn it into Knockdown or Stun. Matches the game's recommendations for Ornette, Sion and Ryza. Thunderrush's 3-piece needs Signal skills, so use them often. Alt: Ryza for Tarte or Sion (build her like Tarte), one swap at a time.

TEAM_DATA.name: Frostbite — Frost
tags: Main DPS + Frost sub-DPS + shield / buffer
TEAM_DATA.note: Othello is the main damage dealer on Frozen targets, Cerese starts Frost and adds crowd control, and Dana supports with Chako's shield and a +10% team Defense aura. All three stack Frost and the team matches the game's recommendations, but patch 1.1.0 lowered Othello's and Cerese's damage and Super Armor break (Dana's damage went up, with higher Rage costs), and their listed damage is the lowest of any full team, so pick it for safety. Alts: Ornette (the game recommends her with Othello; Shock and Knockdown) for Cerese; Alex as a Knockdown tank for Dana.

TEAM_DATA.name: Breaker — Break + Stun
tags: Main DPS / Break starter + Stun sub-DPS + healer
TEAM_DATA.note: Castella is the main damage dealer and Break starter (Stun Blow into Upper Blow), Astria adds Stun and Break damage, and Lute heals and Stuns. Matches the game's recommendation for Castella. Not A because only Castella is A tier. Alts: Theresia (Stun damage) for Astria; Kalien (the game recommends her with Castella and Astria; Stun and Burn) for Lute.

TEAM_DATA.name: Crushing — Knockdown
TEAM_DATA.note: Built around Alex, the only Crushing hero: he tanks with Taunt and his counter cuts the target's Defense by 20%. Othello (Ice Crown, Ice Grab) and Sion (Divine Smash, Justice Fall) both inflict Knockdown, which unlocks Alex's Pounding Grab. This is exactly the game's recommendation for Alex. Othello has no Frost partner here, so his Frozen-only skills fire less often. Alts: Ornette (Shock and Knockdown), Castella (Break starter) or Roxy (Bleed damage) for Othello; Lute (healer, Stun) or Dana (shield) for Sion.

TEAM_DATA.name: Amplitude — Stun
TEAM_DATA.note: Theresia is the main damage dealer (Stun from Celestial Verdict into Divine Arc and Holy Rise), Astria adds Stun and Break damage, and Lute heals and Stuns. Three Stun sources keep Divine Arc and Bolt Bombard live, and Lute's heal makes it the safest Stun team. Matches the game's recommendations for Lute and Theresia. Alt: Roxy (the game recommends her with both Lute and Theresia) for Astria when you want more damage.

He's a partner more than a lead: Charlotte's kit has the bigger finisher ([[skill:Charlotte/Shadow Grab]], 1700%), so Johnny's job is to keep both statuses up for her.

summary: Charlotte is a Venom main damage dealer who plays like an assassin: she Poisons the target, launches it with [[skill:Illusion Kick]] and finishes with [[skill:Shadow Grab]] (1700%), one of the biggest hits in the game. She is **S tier at every stage**, and she leads the S-tier Venom team, which is the game's own recommendation for her.

What makes her special is that she can start her combo on her own. Illusion Kick works on a Poisoned target **or** from her own Stealth ([[skill:Invisible]]), so she never has to wait for a teammate to unlock her skills. Every hit she lands on a Poisoned, Airborne enemy gets the measured status bonuses (+50% for Poison, +100% for Airborne), so her finisher lands at about 2.5× its normal damage.
Her weak spot is Poison uptime: only [[skill:Poison Step]] and [[skill:Poison Dagger]] apply it, so she keeps it up best next to [[hero:Johnny]]. Her A3 pull-in also does nothing against a lone boss.

verdict.label: Yes, a top pick
text: She is one of only three heroes rated S at every stage, she's a Main DPS, and her team is the strongest Venom setup in the guide. If you're spending **Fate's Invitations** in the Hero shop, she is one of the safest choices.
She works at A0 thanks to her self-sufficient combo. Her most valuable awakening is [[awk:5]] (about +17% damage); [[awk:1]] adds a big shuriken to Poison Dagger, a skill she uses all the time.

AWAKENINGS.note: Awakening names and text copied word for word from the in-game screenshots in assets/awakenings/<Hero>/A1-A6.png (OCR, then every line checked by eye). '\n' is a line break in the game text. 'effects' lists the always-on stat bonuses in the same stat names as GEAR_STATS; they count in the end-game totals (purple) and in the build optimiser. Ratings 0-5: kit-changing awakenings are Claude's judgement of what they do for the hero's kit, role and teams. Stat awakenings on damage heroes (28 Oct 2026, after the damage tests) are rated by their modelled damage gain at end-game with the recommended build: 15%+ = 4, 8-15% = 3, 3-8% = 2, 1-3% = 1. The model uses the measured damage rules in DAMAGE_TESTS, assumes the hero's own damage-over-time status stays on the target, counts Airborne/Knockdown/Stun bonuses only on skills that need that status (a lower bound), values Break bonuses at nothing (Break uptime unknown) and values Defense Ignore on an enemy like the Training Ogre (its Defense halves damage). Support and tank heroes' stat awakenings keep their earlier ratings. The best awakening is the highest-rated; on a tie the earlier pick stays.

SKILL_LEVEL_MULTIPLIERS.note: Skill attack weight at each level = Lv.1 weight x multiplier, where Lv.1 = max-level value / 1.75. All levels measured in-game (28 Oct 2026) on 7 skills from 5 heroes (see measured); the multipliers are the same for every hero. Max level 10: Skill, Ultimate, Special A, Special B. Max level 7: Auto, Dash and Jump attacks. Dash (dodge) stays Lv.1; Mastery (passive) can't be levelled. The game rounds a hidden unrounded Lv.1 value x multiplier to the nearest whole %; one hidden value per skill reproduces all 57 measured values exactly. The page only knows the max-level value, so it uses round(max / 1.75 x multiplier): 47 of 57 exact, the other 10 are 1 off.

A piece can't have the same stat as main and substat (flat and % count as different stats). Helmet, Gloves and Boots are currently identical.

observedBlue.note: Blue pieces David wore in the 28 Oct damage tests, compared with the Orange tables. Substats are not one ratio: Critical Hit Resistance, Defense Up and Max HP Up are half of Orange (2.48 vs 4.94, 2.10 vs 4.21, 2.24 vs 4.48), but Defense Ignore is a quarter (0.97 vs 3.88 on boots; screenshot of Battle Will Boots +6). HERO_STAT_MODEL.note: Lv.70 base stats (no gear, no Karma). Estimated until measured in-game: replace a hero's numbers in HERO_BASE_STATS and set 'estimated' to false. Every hero levels the same; only breakthrough bonuses differ by hero. Crit comes only from gear, Karma and buffs.

levelCurve.formula: a + b*(exp(r*(L-1)) - 1); least-squares fit to Lv1, Lv10, Lv20, Lv30 (largest error 0.7 Attack, 0.3 Defense, 5 Max HP). A quadratic fits worse (1.1 / 0.4 / 7). Level 40 will decide: this curve predicts 371 / 103 / 2402 before breakthrough bonuses.

HERO_STAT_MODEL.profileRule: Profile A only for Charlotte (measured); profile B for everyone else. Castella (Main DPS) and Lute (healer) both measured as B, so the profile is not tied to role.

observations.statusResistance: Every status resistance (Stun, Airborne, Knockdown, Shock, Frost, Burn, Poison, Bleed) is 50 on Charlotte with no gear; the same at Lv1.
observations.critRateText: In-game: 'Increases the chance of a Critical Hit ... The final probability is determined by the target's Critical Hit Resistance.' Nothing says what happens above 100%.
observations.setBonusTest: Ballad of Life on Charlotte (no other gear stats, no Karma): Max HP 1975 -> 2152 with 2 pieces (+9%) -> 2271 with 3 pieces (+15% = 2-piece + 3-piece) -> 2271 with 5 pieces. Displayed values are rounded down.
observations.titles: Titles (achievement rewards, Mercenary Crew > Title) give passive bonuses to every hero, slotted or not. The end-game totals don't include titles yet: their effects are only known for these 3.

Flat bonuses are added to the hero's flat stats before % bonuses multiply; % bonuses join the same pool as gear and set % (confirmed in-game: Charlotte Lv30 86 Defense -> (86 + 10) x 1.015 = 97; 1925 Max HP -> 1925 + 50 = 1975, and Ballad of Life's +9%/+15% then apply to 1975). DAMAGE_TESTS.note: Training-dummy results (Lv.90 Training Ogre; the game shows no dummy stats). Every value repeated 5 times with identical results unless noted. Not used by the page yet.
findings: Damage is proportional to Attack: Charlotte's auto-attack hits fell by the same ratio as her Attack (684 -> 637, x0.931; e.g. 3rd click 454 -> 423).
Damage is proportional to the skill %: Shadow Dance Lv.1 -> Lv.2 (332% -> 365%, x1.10) raised every hit by x1.10 (e.g. 423 -> 465).
Crit hit = non-crit x (1 + Critical Damage): x1.5 at 50% Crit Damage; x1.6 during Invisible at Lv.1 (+10%). Each hit of a multi-hit attack rolls its own crit.
Single hit (Reina Wind Slayer Lv.1, 549%, Attack 333): 916 damage = 0.50 x Attack x skill %. Whether the 0.50 is the dummy's defence, a level gap or a fixed constant is not known.

Auto-attack combos match the codex % at 0.50 x Attack when Charlotte's 4th click is counted as one hit (it sometimes hits once, likely an extra hit on the big ogre): Charlotte 0.502-0.505 in all four tests, Reina 0.498 (Wind Sword Lv.2, 385%: 2x89 + 128 + 128 + 205). So the codex % is the whole combo, and the dummy gives the same 0.50 to single hits and combos.

Status ticks (Poison, Bleed, Burn, Shock) = 50% of the applier's Attack, rounded down, 4 ticks per application: Poison 684 -> 342, 637 -> 318, 658 -> 329, Johnny 584 -> 292; Bleed (Roxy), Burn (Aria) and Shock (Ornette) all 71 -> 35 and 326 -> 163. Armor Penetration and Defense Ignore don't change ticks. Frost/Stun/other statuses not tested. Time between ticks not measured.
Skill buffs scale with level too: Invisible's Critical Damage buff is +10% at Lv.1 and +15% at Lv.10 (x1.5, not x1.75).

Armor Penetration raises damage, so the Training Ogre has Defense: at the same 681 Attack, going from 10 to 33 raised the larger hits by 1.2% (499 -> 505, 312 -> 316, 174 -> 176), about +0.05% damage per point against this dummy. Combo ratio 0.505 -> 0.513 x Attack x skill %. The Poison tick stayed 340 (= Attack / 2), so Poison ignores Defense, or at least Armor Penetration. The dummy's Defense value and the exact Defense formula are not known.

Defense Ignore 0.97% (Armor Penetration 0) raised the larger hits by about 0.4% compared with the Armor Penetration 0 tests scaled to the same Attack (e.g. 482 vs 480.3 expected). Combo ratio 0.508. Poison tick 329 = 658 / 2 rounded down, unaffected. Against this dummy, roughly 1% Defense Ignore ~ +0.4% damage and 1 Armor Penetration ~ +0.05%.

Poison tick by stacks, as a share of the FIRST applier's Attack: 1 stack 50%, 2 stacks 75%, 3 stacks 100% (+25% per extra stack). The other appliers' Attack doesn't matter. 2 stacks: Charlotte (658) first -> 493, Johnny (645) first -> 484, whoever applied the second. 3 stacks (goblin dummies, order not tracked): ticks of 645 and 658, exactly the two heroes' Attack. Poison stops at 3 stacks (no 4th). Stacks last about 10 seconds (timed by eye), so the 4 ticks are about 2.5 seconds apart. Bleed, Burn and Shock stack exactly the same way, also to a maximum of 3 (Lv.1 heroes, 71 Attack: 35 / 53 / 71). They also last about 10 seconds (a tick every ~2.5 s).

Burn Additional Damage (+4%) and Burn Additional Attack Power (+110) don't change Burn ticks: Aria with 381 Attack ticked 190 / 285 / 381 = 50 / 75 / 100% of 381, rounded down. So these status bonuses must do something else, most likely raise hits against enemies that have the status (not tested yet).

Hits on an enemy that has Poison, Burn, Bleed or Shock deal x1.5, at any stack count: Charlotte 22 -> 33 with Poison, Roxy 24 -> 36 with Bleed, Ornette 17 -> 26 with Shock; Aria with no Karma (71 Attack) hit 19 on a clean goblin and 28 on a burning one (19.x x 1.5 = 28.5, rounded down), the same at 1, 2 or 3 stacks. The Karma results are explained by the status-bonus rule below.

Status hit bonuses add up: +50% for each damage-over-time status (Poison, Bleed, Burn, Shock) and +100% each for Airborne, Knockdown and Stun. Charlotte's small auto-attack hit (22 clean): Poison 33 (x1.5), Poison + Bleed 44 (x2.0), Airborne + Poison 55 (x2.5), Knockdown + Poison + Bleed 66 (x3.0, recheck), Stun + Poison + Bleed 66 (x3.0), Airborne + Knockdown + Poison 77 (x3.5). Reina: Airborne alone x2.0. Exception: Airborne + Knockdown + Poison + Bleed was 77 (x3.5) twice, where adding up gives x4.0, so either x3.5 is a cap or Bleed wasn't on. The two earlier x2.5 results with Poison + Bleed + Airborne/Knockdown were most likely Bleed wearing off. Break not tested.

How the status bonuses work (tested with Burn): a hit on an enemy with the status = k x (Attack + <status> Additional Attack Power) x 1.5 x (1 + <status> Additional Damage). A clean hit is k x Attack, so neither bonus does anything on a clean enemy, and neither changes ticks. One value of k (0.2677-0.2681 for Aria's first auto-attack hit on the goblins) fits all 8 results: no bonus 19 -> 28; +15% 19 -> 32; +4% & +110 102 -> 205; +19% & +110 102 -> 234. With several statuses the bonuses apply to the whole hit: Aria (381 Attack, +110 / +4% Burn) on Bleed + Knockdown + Burn hit 410 = k x 491 x 3.0 x 1.04 (410.1-410.8). Applying them only to Burn's +50% would give about 323. So: hit = k x (Attack + Additional Attack Power of a status the enemy has) x (1 + all status hit bonuses) x (1 + Additional Damage of a status the enemy has). Not tested: bonuses for two different statuses at once (e.g. Burn and Knockdown Additional Damage together: added or multiplied).

STATUS_EFFECTS.note: Shown on character pages (Skills tab) for heroes whose skills inflict one of these statuses. From David's training-dummy tests on 28 Oct 2026 (details in DAMAGE_TESTS).

rules: Each application ticks 4 times over about 10 seconds (about one tick every 2.5 seconds).
Each tick deals a share of the Attack of the hero who applied the FIRST stack. Later stacks make the ticks bigger, even when another hero applies them, but their own Attack doesn't count.
Ticks aren't reduced by the enemy's Defense: Armor Penetration and Defense Ignore don't change them.

While an enemy has this status, hits on it deal 1.5x damage, whatever the stack count. Bonuses from different statuses add up: +50% for each damage-over-time status and +100% each for Airborne, Knockdown and Stun. Measured: Poison + Bleed 2x, Airborne + Poison 2.5x, Knockdown or Stun + Poison + Bleed 3x, Knockdown + Airborne + Poison 3.5x. The highest seen is 3.5x: Knockdown + Airborne + Poison + Bleed was also 3.5x, not 4x. Measured on training dummies.

A status's “Additional Damage” and “Additional Attack Power” bonuses (from Karmas, gear sets, awakenings and substats) don't change its ticks. They raise every hit on an enemy that has the status: Additional Attack Power is added to your Attack, and Additional Damage multiplies the whole hit, including the bonuses from other statuses (tested with Burn: Blazing Flames' +15% turned Aria's 1.5x into 1.72x).
damageOverTime.untested: Not tested yet: bonuses for two different statuses at once (added or multiplied), whether ticks can crit, and Break.

PATCH_NOTES.note: Official patch notes (assets/patch_notes, from Steam), with developer messages left out and the important changes kept. Dates and BuildIDs are from SteamDB as David sent them. PATCH_NOTES.rating: 1.1.0 hero ratings come from the official before/after numbers. Base damage values are the patch notes' Lv. 1 multipliers × 175, which equals the codex max-level % (124 of 126 match exactly; the other 2 are Alex's two basic attacks, whose names the notes swap). damagePct is the change in the sum of every damaging skill's max-level %. Direction: buff or nerf when that sum moves 3% or more; if Rage, status-application or Super Armor changes point the other way it's mixed. Under 3%, if one skill went up 15% or more and another went down 15% or more, damage was moved between skills and it's mixed, with impact from the share moved (half the sum of all skill changes, as a % of the total; same 5% and 10% bands). Otherwise under 3% the non-damage changes decide, and with none it's adjusted. Impact: under 5% Minor, 5–10% Moderate, 10% or more Major, one step higher when 2 or more non-damage changes point the same way. Crit buff values changed by the crit rework aren't counted. Ratings for other patches are read from the notes, with no numbers given.

patches.headline: Combat rework: new damage formula, crit and Defense Ignore reworks, skill changes for all 19 existing heroes, new hero Ryza, Training Ground and Hell Hunts.

highlights.text: New hero Ryza (Thunderbolt, Shock), a reward for Adventure Quest 53. Reunion. Her Exclusive Karma The Scar Lightning Left Behind is at the Exchange.

Crit rework: crits now happen exactly at your Critical Rate, and monsters no longer have critical resistance, so 100% Critical Rate means every hit crits. Crit values on gear and skills were adjusted to keep the same feel.
Defense Ignore rework: displayed damage numbers are lower, but monster Max HP was reduced in proportion to their Defense (up to 44% on giant bosses), so time-to-kill is about the same.

New gear Sub-Option "Status Effect Additional Attack Power Increase": raises every status Additional Attack Power by the option value (%). That bonus is added to your Attack against enemies with the matching status.

Skill damage and Rage costs adjusted for every hero to fit the new formula, with underperforming heroes raised. Castella's Rage efficiency was raised, some heroes' Super Armor break lowered, and the multi-mount damage bonus was increased by 20%.
Training Ground added (Edric, in front of Roderic Palace): stationary Ogre dummy or combat-active Ogre or Goblin, with total damage and DPS.
Hunt Score & Rank system, a sixth Hunt difficulty (Hell), and lower monster stats on Nightmare. Clear times now start when combat begins.
Othello's Hero Quest What the Wind Asks (after Chapter 5), new stills in Dana's Hero Log, and tracked-quest markers in Scenario Mode.
8 new map pin types, a third cooking Quick Slot, a Tag Combo animation toggle, hero recruitment tutorials, Familiars now obtained from the Codex, and a separate Throw key.
